newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr trapped in tight range, awaits overseas events.
newsitem.headline: Dlr trapped in tight range, awaits overseas events.

text.p: 0615 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar was confined to a narrow range against the yen by late Tokyo trade on Tuesday, sandwiched between talk of exporter offers and bids from trust banks and Japanese investors below 118 yen, dealers said.
The market awaited the Bundesbank's announcement on money market operations and a U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later in the day.
"The market lacked trading incentives in dollar/yen trade alone," a city bank dealer said.
Although a majority of traders expect no rate changes at either the FOMC meeting or from Buba, they said they remained cautious about confirming such an outcome.

"With a shaky U.S. stock market and ahead of many events, such as the release of M3 in Germany and the Bundesbank's council meeting on August 21, trade remained directionless in Tokyo," a dealer at a European bank said.
Dealers said buying back of marks against the yen indirectly supported the greenback against the yen.

But the city bank dealer said Japanese exporters gradually became eager to place offers near 65 yen after an upside probe above 65 yen had failed on Monday, keeping the mark's topside heavy versus the yen.
The mark was quoted at around 64.42/45 yen at 0627 GMT, compared with 64.35 yen in late New York on Monday.
Exporters were still inactive for most of Tokyo trade, but dealers said they were keen to sell dollars above 118.50 yen.
Despite steady bids just below 118 yen, a lack of follow-through buying incentives limited the dollar's advance, they said.

Dealers said they were also focusing on moves in U.S. stocks later in New York trade after the Dow pared Friday's large losses and ended up over 100 points on Monday, for a clue to whether U.S. stocks would continue to recover.

News that United Parcel Service (UPS) had reached a tentative pact with the Teamsters union to end a 15-day strike had limited direct impact on currencies. But dealers said they would cautiously watch moves in U.S. Treasuries later in U.S. markets as the UPS news might raise concerns about wage inflation in the United States and could depress bond prices.

The dollar was also traded narrowly against the mark as traders awaited the next German auction for securities repurchase agreements (repos) and Buba's regular policy meeting on Thursday, the first since its four-week summer recess.

Few expected to see a rise or a switch to variable tenders in money market operations later on Tuesday after Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Monday that a rise in German interest rates at the present time would be very damaging to the German economy, dealers said.
